description.html: Interactive installation for L'Atelier Magazine, the annual publication of the EPFL Masters in Architecture. The installation generates a video stream procedurally using Touchdesigner. A QR code next to the work creates a remote on your phone browser.

I worked on an undisclosed research and development project exploring how spatial computing could enhance the in-store product-buying experience. Collaborating with a team of designers and developers, I helped take the concept from observing visitor flows to delivering a functional, interactive prototype.

The process included designing and animating the UI, creating motion studies in After Effects, and translating them into code. The experience made use of presence and proximity detection, along with a custom-trained object detection algorithm, allowing customers to explore products on a large screen simply through their position and movement.

Done at Random Studio, Digital Twin is a research project for a product discovery interface. I explored ways in which the digital layer would allow for deeper insight into product features. The oloid shape was chosen as an abstract object that aimed to make the explorations universal and agnostic of product. So that the interactions / digital environments created could be adapted to any product.
This video features highlights of the process. I made the 3D animations featured in the various prototypes, shooting and editing of the video as well as the sound design.

ELPE is a visual identity project completed at ECAL under the supervision of the head of the Graphic Design department, Angelo Benedetto. The brief was to develop a dynamic visual identity for an iamginary art space. The concept takes the glass lens and utilises its refractive property as an optical typographical effect.

I led the sound design for Glossier’s Fleur fragrance launch in Paris, collaborating closely with their spatial designers and creative team to craft a multi-sensory experience aligned with the campaign's tone. Each of the four perfumes had its own pavilion, and I composed a unique soundscape for each—translating fragrance notes and personality into immersive audio. Random developed an interactive web-tool to preview the sounds which you can find here. A unifying ambient layer connected the entire space.

At the center of the experience was the an interactive AI installation where visitors could experience the new fragrance., where I designed responsive sound to accompany real-time, personalized poetry. This was my first sound project at this scale—an exciting opportunity to explore how sound can transform and elevate spatial storytelling.
For the full case study and more details, please visit this link.

SELF DE / CON / RE STRUCT is a kinetic installation conceived by Kim Winder, which was exhibited at BIG ART, Amsterdam. The work explores the tension between fragmentation and transformation—breaking and reassembling self-portraits in real time. Through generative code and physical movement, the installation invites viewers to engage with shifting identities and the beauty found in imperfection.
My role was to program the installation which is powered by an Arduino
Photos by Kim Winder, Maikel Jay, Jan Willem Kaldenbach.

A Living Entrance is an interactive installation hosted by Het Hem in Zaandam, in collaboration with artist Johannes Offerhaus . It is an internal artistic research project that explores the first impression and how an AI might make one based on our presence in a space.

My role on the project was to research and develop the concept in a collaboration between the artist and Random Studio. I also designed the interface for the web app which controlled the installation and did the sound design for the documentation video.
A research zine was also printed to be handed out at the event. I designed the layout of it and you can find it here. For the full case study, please visit this link.
In collaboration with Industrial Designer Alex Sinh Nguyen, we made the MIDI Clock. The brief was to reimagine, the alarm clock, an object now considered obsolete by many.

We created an alarm clock that generates tomorrow's alarm sound based on geographical data you record during the day. Map direction are translated into MIDI notes and different neighbourhoods unlock different sounds and instruments.

Map direction are translated into MIDI notes and different neighbourhoods unlock different sounds and instruments.
Made in collaboration with Interaction Designer Nathanael Vianin, during a one week workshop with engineers from Mindmaze. We created a visualiser for EEG waves captured with a Unicorn headset.

Made in collaboration with Interaction Designer Tickie Bindner, we created the Physical Sequencer. A device that generates sound based on the distance at which various objects are placed around it. Using a LiDar sensor for data, the device is a Teensy based synth with an onboard battery and speaker which freedom in exploring the sounds one can create with their environment
Targeted at the world of photojournalism, FULCRUM addresses privacy concerns surrounding the publication of photographs.
Whilst many photo-journalists would agree that blurring or censoring faces tampers with important historical documents, protecting sources is ultimately a core journalistic principle.

Given today's ubiquitous data scraping and face detection algorithms, legislation aimed at mitigating potential abuse, remains outpaced by the swift progress of technology. FULCRUM explores an angle in the ethical debate between photojournalists and the public.

By masking subjects' faces with AI generated ones, FULCRUM ensures non-destructive anonymisation, that simultaneously safeguards the identity of the individuals depicted, as well as the photographic quality of the image.

Made in collaboration with Interaction Designer Tickie Bindner during a one week workshop with Yehwan Song. Tasked to create a project that explores the website and the mobile experiences' relationship with the space, we made the connection between the scrollbar of a webpage and the handrail of a set of stairs. We made a phone case that attached to the handrail and transmitted data from a rotary encoder, via wifi, to the web page which would scroll in increments as the user went up the steps. Each step had its own section of the website thus creating a relationship between the physical and the digital.

This is the first website I made. Done at ECAL as a semester project, the brief was to collect data from our daily life. I chose to record road cycling rides through Strava, then transforming the GPS data and elevation into 3D models. I also had my camera with me to take photos as part of the documentation.

For a semester course with Gilliane Cachin, I made a publication about microscopes and microphotography. I created a visual language which interprets graphical elements around the theme, in an attempt to explore their aesthetic potential. The "pseudo-scientific" visual research is laid out in this edition alongside spec sheets of cutting edge microscopes.

title: Stretching Time
description: Made in collaboration with Industrial Designers Denise Merlette, Giulia Burrus and Léa Omez, during a one week workshop on "Soft Electronics" with Claire Eliot. We created three timers that invoke the human perception of time. Each has an approximate interval, between 3-5 minutes, 10-15 or 30-45. The objects leverage the elastic properties of the chosen materials. By sewing a pattern of conductive wire into the fabric, stretching the material varies the resistance the circuit can pick up, which in turn sets the timer.

Made in collaboration with Interaction Designer Antoine Contreras during a one week workshop with Ted Davis. Using a p5.js library that enables cathode ray oscilloscope to reproduce digital canvases. We wanted to create a game, as a sort of hommage to the early days of computing powered by CRT displays. The inherent limited size at which images can be displayed, was leveraged by structuring the game around a small patch of the map. Furthermore we reward the user for trying to break the rules, this is a maze game which allows you to pass through the walls of the maze, however decreasing the frequency of the display at each pass, thus making it harder to see the map.

During a one week workshop with Zach Lieberman I got to learn how to use OpenFrameworks. Having long wanted to explore GLSL and shaders, I concentrated by week's efforts on adding interaction to these realtime sketches themed around the circle.
Random Studio designed this exhibition for Zara’s headquarters in Galicia, Spain; an in-house exhibition that inspires and educates staff on the creative potential of recycled fabrics.

My role was to design the sound for the exhibition space, in collaboration with the team of architects at Random and the client, we developed this sound loop to accentuate and compliment the spatial experience.
